No late-night bar hopping or clubs

trip_paths.name: Slow-Paced Wine & Dine
trip_paths.vibe_summary: Long mornings at the rental, one winery or activity per day max, group dinners by 7pm, everyone in bed by 11.
trip_paths.who_it_fits: Best for the 2 of you who want to truly unplug. You'll have built-in porch time every afternoon.

lodging_guidance.recommendation: Book a 3-bedroom rental in Yountville or St. Helena — both are walkable to tasting rooms and restaurants
lodging_guidance.why_this_works: Central location means less driving. Shared kitchen lets you do casual breakfasts together. Outdoor space for morning coffee and evening wine.
what_to_look_for: Outdoor patio or deck (essential for this vibe)
Full kitchen — you'll want to make breakfast
At least 2 full bathrooms for 5 people
Walking distance to at least one restaurant
avoid: Properties that require a car for everything
Places with shared walls or strict quiet hours

suggested_experiences.name: Morning walk through Yountville + pastries at Bouchon Bakery
suggested_experiences.why: Low-key start that doesn't require reservations or scheduling
suggested_experiences.timing: Any morning, whenever you wake up

suggested_experiences.name: Seated tasting at a boutique vineyard (Tres Sabores or Frog's Leap)
suggested_experiences.why: Smaller wineries, less crowded, can accommodate shellfish allergy with notice

suggested_experiences.name: Spa afternoon at Calistoga (mud baths or massage)
suggested_experiences.why: Hits the relaxation priority, and gives the group a shared experience

suggested_experiences.name: Farm-to-table dinner at Farmstead or Bottega
suggested_experiences.why: Both have excellent shellfish-free options and fit the food-focused vibe

sample_day.label: What Day 2 Actually Looks Like
sample_day.morning: Wake up naturally (no alarms). Make coffee, eat yogurt and pastries on the patio. Chat until 10am.
sample_day.midday: Drive 15 min to your 11am winery appointment. Seated tasting for 90 minutes. Back by 1pm.
sample_day.afternoon: Free time. Some people nap, some read by the pool, someone walks into town for shopping.
sample_day.evening: Everyone regroups at 6pm. Get ready together. Walk to dinner at 7pm. Home by 10pm for nightcap on the porch.

booking_priorities.why_book_early: Good 3-bedrooms in Yountville book up 4-6 weeks out for weekends
booking_priorities.when_to_book: This week, once you confirm dates

booking_priorities.why_book_early: Farmstead and Bottega fill up 2-3 weeks ahead for Saturday nights
booking_priorities.when_to_book: As soon as you have the rental confirmed

booking_priorities.why_book_early: Weekend spa slots go fast, especially for groups

budget_estimate.notes: 2 nice dinners, casual lunches, wine at tastings

tradeoffs: Less variety — you'll do fewer activities than other paths
Rental means shared bathrooms and less privacy
The person who wants more structure might feel antsy by Day 2
trip_paths.who_might_feel_meh: The one person who wanted a structured plan might feel like 'we're not doing anything' — build in one anchor activity per day to give them something to look forward to.
watchouts: Book wineries that don't require driving between — or use rideshare
Confirm shellfish allergy accommodations when making dinner reservations
Bring card games or a speaker — you'll have a lot of porch time

trip_paths.name: Curated Highlights Weekend
trip_paths.vibe_summary: One planned experience each morning, free afternoons, elevated group dinners. Feels purposeful but not rushed.
trip_paths.who_it_fits: Good middle ground: enough structure for the planner, enough downtime for the chill crew.

lodging_guidance.recommendation: Book rooms at a boutique hotel like Bardessono or Hotel Yountville — walkable to restaurants, no cooking required
lodging_guidance.why_this_works: Everyone gets their own space at night. Hotel handles breakfast. Pool access for afternoon downtime.
what_to_look_for: Book rooms on the same floor or adjoining if possible
Concierge that can help with winery bookings
avoid: Chain hotels outside of town — you'll lose the walkability
Properties without common spaces for group hangs

suggested_experiences.name: Group cooking class at CIA at Copia
suggested_experiences.why: Hands-on, food-focused, and gives the structured planners a clear anchor activity
suggested_experiences.timing: Day 1, 10am-1pm (arrive day before or early morning)

suggested_experiences.name: Private tour at Stag's Leap or Opus One
suggested_experiences.why: Elevated experience that feels special — worth the splurge for a group trip

suggested_experiences.name: Sunset hot air balloon ride (optional splurge)
suggested_experiences.why: Once-in-a-lifetime experience, but only if budget allows

suggested_experiences.name: Fancy dinner at The French Laundry or Auberge
suggested_experiences.why: If this is a special occasion, this is the meal you'll remember

sample_day.label: What Day 2 Actually Looks Like
sample_day.morning: Breakfast at the hotel (included). Meet in lobby at 10:15am for the 11am winery tour.
sample_day.midday: Private tour and tasting finishes around 1pm. Grab lunch in town (casual, $25-35/person).
sample_day.afternoon: Free until 5pm. Some people pool, some explore shops, one person takes a nap.
sample_day.evening: Meet at 5:30pm to get ready. Dinner reservation at 6:30pm. Drinks after at the hotel bar.

booking_priorities.why_book_early: Boutique hotels in Yountville have limited inventory — book 6+ weeks out
CIA classes fill up, especially weekends
booking_priorities.when_to_book: As soon as hotel is confirmed

booking_priorities.why_book_early: French Laundry books 2 months out. Auberge books 3-4 weeks out.
booking_priorities.when_to_book: Immediately for French Laundry; 3 weeks out for others

budget_estimate.notes: 2 per room at a boutique hotel
Hotel may offer shuttle; otherwise rideshare

tradeoffs: Higher cost overall — this path runs $1,200-1,800 per person
Less group hang time in the mornings (no rental kitchen vibes)
More logistics to coordinate with scheduled activities
trip_paths.who_might_feel_meh: The 2 cost-conscious folks might feel the pinch. Consider offering optional activities so people can opt out of the $300 balloon ride without FOMO.
watchouts: Make sure everyone is aligned on the splurge dinner — it's not for everyone
Build buffer time between activities — Napa traffic is real
Confirm dietary accommodations when booking cooking class and restaurants

Make dinner reservations 2-3 weeks out for Saturday night
Create a shared note or group chat for trip planning once path is picked
